frame: Mars body-fixed: east longitude 0–360°, planetocentric latitude. Each orbit sample = the point on Mars directly under the moon + centre-to-centre distance.

orbits.encoding: uint16 triplets: lon = v/65536·360, lat = int16(v)/100, distance km = base + v/10

shape.encoding: int16 metres added to radius; row 0 = lat 90°, col 0 = lon −180°, 1° steps

photo.mapping: simple cylindrical, lon −180° at the left edge, east-positive

credits: Phobos shape: Mars Express HRSC Instrument Team / Europlanet — Phobos HRSC DEM Global 100 m (Willner et al. 2010, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2009.07.033), USGS Astrogeology
Phobos photo: P. Stooke — Phobos Viking Global Mosaic 5 m, DLR-controlled (Wählisch et al. 2010), USGS Astrogeology
Orbits: NASA/JPL Horizons (Solar System Dynamics Group)
